new.title: Tour the cathedral and cloister of Saint-Bertrand
new.desc: The Notre-Dame cathedral of Saint-Bertrand-de-Comminges was built from the 11th century onward under Bishop Bertrand de l'Isle. Its cloister combines one Romanesque gallery with three Gothic ones, with carved capitals, and opens onto the Pyrenean hillside.
new.tip: The paid visit covers the cloister, the canons' choir and the treasury; a duo ticket adds the basilica of Valcabrère. Allow two hours for the village too.
new.q: Cathédrale Notre-Dame de Saint-Bertrand-de-Comminges, Saint-Bertrand-de-Comminges

new.title: Visit the Romanesque basilica of Saint-Just de Valcabrère
new.desc: This Romanesque church about a kilometre from Saint-Bertrand has been on the UNESCO list since 1998 as part of the Camino de Santiago routes. Pilgrims once stopped here to venerate the relics of Saints Just and Pasteur before going on to the cathedral.
new.tip: Walk the path from Saint-Bertrand in about 20 minutes. A duo ticket links the basilica with the cathedral.
new.q: Basilique Saint-Just de Valcabrère, Valcabrère

new.title: See the Saint-Ferréol dam that feeds the Canal du Midi
new.desc: The Bassin de Saint-Ferréol was built under Pierre-Paul Riquet in the 1660s and 1670s to supply the Canal du Midi with water from the Montagne Noire, and was later enlarged under Vauban. It was the first dam built specifically to feed a navigable canal and is part of the UNESCO-listed canal system.
new.tip: The Reservoir discovery centre next to the lake explains the engineering. The lake park is free to enter.
new.q: Bassin de Saint-Ferréol, Vaudreuille, Revel

new.title: Admire the 14th-century covered hall of Revel
new.desc: Revel is a bastide founded by Philippe VI de Valois in 1342 around a central square. Its medieval hall is about 39 metres on each side and is held up by 79 oak pillars, topped by a neo-classical belfry from 1834.
new.tip: Come on a Saturday morning when the market fills the hall. Ask the tourist office about belfry visits, as the belfry was under restoration.
new.q: Halle de Revel, Place Philippe VI de Valois, Revel

new.title: Stand beneath the castle of Saint-Félix-Lauragais
new.desc: The castle on its rocky spur has buildings from the 13th to the 18th centuries and is attested in the archives from 1032. Tradition links the village to the Cathar Council of Saint-Félix of 1167 and to its capture by Simon de Montfort in 1211.
new.tip: Guided visits start from the tourist office on Rue des Écoles; check the hours as the castle is privately owned.
new.q: Château de Saint-Félix-Lauragais, Rue des Écoles, Saint-Félix-Lauragais

new.title: Find the octagonal tower of Rieux-Volvestre cathedral
new.desc: The former cathedral Sainte-Marie was the seat of the bishopric of Rieux from 1317 until the Concordat of 1801. Its five-storey octagonal bell tower is a 15th-century work, and a carved early-Renaissance door from about 1530 let bishops walk in from their palace.
new.tip: Open during tourist office hours, with guided visits in July and August. The episcopal treasure is shown on the same visit.
new.q: Ancienne cathédrale Sainte-Marie, Rieux-Volvestre

new.title: Marvel at Albi's brick cathedral Sainte-Cécile
new.desc: Begun in 1282 and completed in 1390, Sainte-Cécile is often called the largest brick cathedral in the world and is part of the UNESCO-listed Episcopal City of Albi. Inside are painted vaults, with the decoration of the vault dating from 1509.
new.tip: The nave is free; the choir and the Last Judgement area have an admission fee. Visit in the morning for the best light on the vault.
new.q: Cathédrale Sainte-Cécile, Place Sainte-Cécile, Albi

new.title: Meet Toulouse-Lautrec in the Berbie Palace
new.desc: The Palais de la Berbie is a fortified 13th-century archbishops' palace that has housed the Musée Toulouse-Lautrec since 1922. It holds the most important public collection devoted to the painter, who was born in Albi.
new.tip: The palace gardens are worth a visit in their own right. Entry through the porch on Place de l'Archevêché avoids the stairs.
new.q: Musée Toulouse-Lautrec, Palais de la Berbie, Place Sainte-Cécile, Albi

new.title: Cross the Pont Vieux for the view of the Berbie
new.desc: The Pont Vieux over the Tarn dates from the 11th century and is one of the oldest bridges in France still in use. It gives a classic view of the cathedral, the Berbie palace and the old city reflected in the river.
new.tip: Go at dusk when the brick glows. Check that the bridge is open to pedestrians, as it was closed for a time after Tarn floods.
new.q: Pont Vieux, Albi

new.title: Climb the Grand Rue Raimond VII in Cordes-sur-Ciel
new.desc: Cordes was founded in 1222 by Raymond VII, Count of Toulouse, as a hilltop bastide. The upper town keeps noble houses with carved facades such as the Grand Écuyer, Grand Veneur and Grand Fauconnier, and the 13th-century Porte des Ormeaux.
new.tip: Park at the bottom and climb on foot, or take the little tourist train in season. Many cobbled slopes, so wear flat shoes.
new.q: Grand Rue Raimond VII, Cordes-sur-Ciel

new.title: Photograph the houses on the Agout in Castres
new.desc: The colourful houses overhanging the Agout were the workshops of tanners, parchment-makers and textile workers, with roots in the late 12th century. Renovated from 1974, they became the emblem of Castres, nicknamed the little Venice of Languedoc.
new.tip: Best seen from the Pont Vieux or the Place de l'Albinque banks in the morning. Free all year.
new.q: Maisons sur l'Agout, Quai des Jacobins, Castres

new.title: See Goya and the Le Nôtre garden in Castres
new.desc: The Musée Goya occupies the former bishops' palace and holds the main collection of Hispanic art in France after the Louvre. Beside it lies the Jardin de l'Évêché, a French garden laid out from 1676 for Bishop Maupeou and attributed to André Le Nôtre.
new.tip: The garden is free and open daily. The museum is on Rue de l'Hôtel de Ville next to the town hall.
new.q: Musée Goya, Jardin de l'Évêché, Place de la République, Castres

new.title: Visit Lautrec and its working windmill
new.desc: Lautrec is a Plus Beau Village known for its pink garlic and its 15th-century covered market hall. The Moulin à vent de La Salette above the village, dated to 1688 in one source, was restored in 1991 and can still produce flour.
new.tip: The garlic festival falls on the first Friday of August. Check the tourist office for windmill opening days.
new.q: Moulin à vent de La Salette, Lautrec

new.title: Walk the ramparts of Puycelsi
new.desc: Puycelsi is a fortified Plus Beau Village on a ridge at the edge of the Grésigne forest, with about 800 metres of ramparts and houses from the 14th and 15th centuries. Its church of Saint-Corneille is a listed monument.
new.tip: The walk around the walls takes about 30 minutes. Park below the village; the car is the practical way to arrive.
new.q: Remparts de Puycelsi, Puycelsi

new.title: Stand on the Place des Arcades in Castelnau-de-Montmiral
new.desc: This bastide was founded in the 13th century by Raymond VII and is considered the little sister of Cordes. Its central square is framed by brick, stone and half-timbered houses on pointed arches, with an old well and a medieval pillory.
new.tip: A morning market is held on the square (a Tuesday market is reported). The Hôtel des Consuls and a cafe sit on the square.
new.q: Place des Arcades, Castelnau-de-Montmiral

new.title: Spot the Peyro Clabado balanced rock at Sidobre
new.desc: The Sidobre is a granite plateau of about 100 square kilometres east of Castres. The Peyro Clabado is a balanced boulder of some 780 tonnes resting on a base of roughly one square metre, and is the emblem of Lacrouzette.
new.tip: A short walk from the road; the Sidobre has many more boulder fields such as the Chaos de la Resse.
new.q: Peyro Clabado, Lacrouzette

new.title: Look down on the Tarn loop at Ambialet
new.desc: The Benedictine priory of Ambialet sits at 295 metres at the top of a peninsula that a meander of the Tarn wraps around for three kilometres. Monks from Marseille founded it in 1057. The priory itself is private, but the viewpoint along the Stations of the Cross is open.
new.tip: Climb the path from the village for the view of the meander. Free access all year.
new.q: Prieuré d'Ambialet, Ambialet

new.title: Discover Ingres drawings in Montauban
new.desc: The Musée Ingres Bourdelle in the former episcopal palace holds about 4,500 drawings and 44 paintings by Ingres, the largest collection of his drawings in the world. It reopened on 13 December 2019 with a larger Bourdelle sculpture section.
new.tip: Free on the first Sunday of each month. It stands next to the brick Place Nationale.
new.q: Musée Ingres Bourdelle, 19 Rue de l'Hôtel de Ville, Montauban

new.title: Study the Romanesque cloister of Moissac abbey
new.desc: The cloister of the abbey of Saint-Pierre, built around 1100, has 76 carved capitals, about fifty of them historiated with scenes such as the death of John the Baptist and Saint Martin sharing his cloak. It is part of the UNESCO Camino de Santiago listing of 1998.
new.tip: Allow time for the carved porch of the abbey church as well. Book guided visits in summer.
new.q: Abbaye Saint-Pierre de Moissac, Place Durand de Bredons, Moissac

new.title: See the Romanesque town hall of Saint-Antonin-Noble-Val
new.desc: The old town hall, or Maison romane, is one of the oldest civic buildings in France, dated to the early 12th century. Viollet-le-Duc visited in 1842 and its restoration followed from 1846 to 1853; it now houses a museum and has a belfry.
new.tip: Visit on a Sunday market morning when the town is at its liveliest. The museum can be visited with a ticket.
new.q: Maison romane, Place de la Halle, Saint-Antonin-Noble-Val

new.title: Explore the castles of Bruniquel above the Aveyron
new.desc: Two castles stand on a rocky spur nearly 100 metres above the Aveyron gorges. The Château Vieux has a Renaissance gallery looking out over a 90-metre drop, and both were used to film Le Vieux Fusil (1975).
new.tip: The village is a Plus Beau Village; allow time to walk its lanes. Check opening hours as visits are seasonal.
new.q: Châteaux de Bruniquel, Bruniquel

new.title: Wander medieval Caylus and its stained glass
new.desc: Caylus is a fortified medieval village on the slopes of the Bonnette valley. Its church of Saint-Jean-Baptiste, a listed monument, holds what one guide calls the finest ensemble of old stained glass in Tarn-et-Garonne.
new.tip: The church is on Rue Droite. Pair with a drive along the nearby Gorges de l'Aveyron.
new.q: Église Saint-Jean-Baptiste, Rue Droite, Caylus

new.title: Visit the round grain hall of Auvillar
new.desc: Auvillar is a Plus Beau Village above the Garonne on the Santiago route. Its circular grain hall on a triangular square rests on Tuscan-style columns, dated to 1825 or 1830, and is considered unique in the south-west.
new.tip: The Tour de l'Horloge gate is a few steps away. The village is brick-red at sunset.
new.q: Halle aux grains, Place de la Halle, Auvillar

new.title: Sit under the arcades of Lauzerte's Place des Cornières
new.desc: Lauzerte is a hilltop bastide in the Quercy Blanc and a Plus Beau Village on a Santiago route. Its Place des Cornières, about 35 by 30 metres, has arcades on three sides and half-timbered houses, with a raised paving corner by ceramicist Jacques Buchholtz (1988).
new.tip: The Saturday morning market is held on the square. Church of Saint-Barthélemy is next door.
new.q: Place des Cornières, Lauzerte

new.title: Climb the towers of the Château de Foix
new.desc: The castle of the counts of Foix, with three towers, houses the departmental Ariège museum since 1930. Two of the towers can be climbed for views over the town and the Pyrenees.
new.tip: The guided ground-floor tour lasts about 45 minutes. Check seasonal hours on the official Ariège sites page.
new.q: Château de Foix, Rue du Château, Foix

new.title: See the timber arcades of Mirepoix
new.desc: The central square of this bastide, the Place des Couverts, is lined with half-timbered houses on wooden pillars forming the arcades called couverts. The Maison des Consuls, with carved beams, and the broad-naved cathedral Saint-Maurice stand close by.
new.tip: A Monday morning market fills the square. Medieval festivals are held in summer.
new.q: Place des Couverts, Mirepoix

new.title: Climb to the Cathar castle of Montségur
new.desc: The ruined castle perches on a peak of about 1,207 metres, the pog, and fell after a siege of roughly a year in 1243 or 1244. The village museum at 32 rue du Village goes with the castle ticket.
new.tip: The climb takes about 30 minutes from the car park (170 m of ascent). Wear sturdy shoes, and check current prices.
new.q: Château de Montségur, Montségur

new.title: Descend to the Salon Noir of the Niaux cave
new.desc: The cave of Niaux holds prehistoric paintings in the Salon Noir, reached after an 800-metre walk in the dark with handheld lamps. The guided visit lasts about 1 hour 40 minutes and groups are small.
new.tip: Online booking is mandatory. Arrive 15 minutes early and bring warm clothes and good shoes.
new.q: Grotte de Niaux, Niaux

new.title: Drive through the Mas-d'Azil cave
new.desc: The Arize river runs through the Mas-d'Azil cave, and so does the D119 road, which makes it unique in Europe. The road crosses the cave for several hundred metres. The cave is also a major prehistoric site.
new.tip: Park at the cave's south entrance and visit on foot with a guide. The visit includes the prehistoric galleries.
new.q: Grotte du Mas-d'Azil, Le Mas-d'Azil

new.title: Visit the cloister and two cathedrals of Saint-Lizier
new.desc: Saint-Lizier has two cathedrals, a 12th-century cloister, the only Romanesque cloister in Ariège, and a bishops' palace built in 1654. The cathedral of Notre-Dame de la Sède sits inside the palace.
new.tip: A combined ticket covers the cloister, treasure and an 18th-century pharmacy. Opening hours are limited, so check the tourist office.
new.q: Cathédrale Notre-Dame de la Sède et cloître, Saint-Lizier

new.title: Dip your feet in the Bassin des Ladres in Ax-les-Thermes
new.desc: The Bassin des Ladres was built in 1260 with the hospital founded by Count Roger IV of Foix and has been a listed monument since 1979. Its thermal water emerges at about 77 degrees.
new.tip: Free and always open, on Place du Breilh, under ten minutes on foot from the station. Bring a towel.
new.q: Bassin des Ladres, Place du Breilh, Ax-les-Thermes

new.title: See sugar sculpture at Yves Thuriès museum in Cordes
new.desc: The Musée des Arts du Sucre et du Chocolat opened in 1989 in the medieval Maison Prunet at 33 Grand Rue Raimond VII. Yves Thuriès, a twice-named Meilleur Ouvrier de France, set it up next to his pastry workshop.
new.tip: The visit ends with a tasting and shop. Sugar-working demonstrations run on weekdays on request.
new.q: Musée des Arts du Sucre et du Chocolat, 33 Grand Rue Raimond VII, Cordes-sur-Ciel

new.title: Eat Tarn home cooking at Lou Sicret in Albi
new.desc: Lou Sicret is a small restaurant in the old quarter of Albi known for traditional Tarn cooking. Reviewers mention the poor man's purée and cassoulet.
new.tip: Book ahead for dinner as the room is tiny. Ask for the cassoulet.
new.q: Lou Sicret, Rue Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec, Albi

new.title: Order cod cassoulet at Le Lautrec in Albi
new.desc: Le Lautrec at 13 rue Toulouse Lautrec occupies the former stables of the painter's birthplace, a short walk from the cathedral. Its menu includes a cod cassoulet.
new.tip: Mains average around 46 euros per person with starter and dessert. Closed some evenings, so confirm hours.
new.q: Le Lautrec, 13 Rue Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec, Albi

new.title: Eat a grill at Resto des Halles in Castres
new.desc: Resto des Halles is a 1950s-style traditional brasserie recreated on the first floor of the Halles de l'Albinque. It uses local produce and is known for its meat.
new.tip: Go on a market morning (Tuesday to Sunday) when the hall below is busy. Reserve at weekends.
new.q: Resto des Halles, Halle de l'Albinque, Castres

new.title: Buy old-style bread at Maison Mauranes in Montauban
new.desc: Maison Mauranes is a baker with a shop in the covered market on Place Nationale. Gault&Millau notes its seasonal pastries, traditional breads, viennoiseries and homemade chocolates.
new.tip: Come in the morning for the bread; market days are busiest.
new.q: Maison Mauranes, Place Nationale, Montauban

new.title: Eat Moissac chasselas dishes at Le Bistrot Gourmand
new.desc: Facing the abbey, this bistro serves Moissac specialities and south-west traditional cooking. Chasselas de Moissac was the first fruit to receive an AOC, in 1971.
new.tip: Menus start around 20 euros. Sit opposite the abbey porch.
new.q: Le Bistrot Gourmand, Place Durand de Bredons, Moissac

new.title: Try home cooking at Brasserie du Marché in Moissac
new.desc: La Brasserie du Marché, also called Chez Isa, serves traditional home cooking on Avenue du Chasselas with a large shaded terrace. The tourism listing shows it open every day through 2026.
new.tip: Try the plat du jour on the terrace. Come after the Saturday market.
new.q: La Brasserie du Marché Chez Isa, 19 Avenue du Chasselas, Moissac

new.title: Eat azinat ariégeois at L'Ostal in Foix
new.desc: L'Ostal serves azinat ariégeois, a cabbage-based mountain stew, as its speciality, alongside pig's ear and cep ravioli gratin.
new.tip: Book at weekends. It is on the Allées de Villote.
new.q: Restaurant L'Ostal, Allées de Villote, Foix

new.title: Taste Mauzac and Ondenc at Domaine Plageoles
new.desc: Domaine Plageoles at Très Cantous, Cahuzac-sur-Vère, works old Gaillac varieties such as Mauzac and Ondenc. It is known for its ancestral-method sparkling Mauzac and a Mauzac aged under a veil.
new.tip: Tasting at the estate; call ahead as hours and prices were not confirmed online.
new.q: Domaine Plageoles, Très Cantous, Cahuzac-sur-Vère

new.title: Eat duck confit at Le Chien Fou in Saint-Antonin
new.desc: Le Chien Fou is a brasserie and bar in the old town of Saint-Antonin-Noble-Val whose signature dish is duck confit. It is open Wednesday to Sunday.
new.tip: Sit on the terrace in the old quarter. Check seasonal hours.
new.q: Le Chien Fou, Saint-Antonin-Noble-Val

new.title: Eat garbure at Le Chalet des Gourmands in Luchon
new.desc: Le Chalet des Gourmands in Bagnères-de-Luchon serves a mountain menu with garbure, raclette, tartiflette, fondue and galettes, with a focus on cheese.
new.tip: Under 20 minutes on foot from the station. Come hungry in winter.
new.q: Le Chalet des Gourmands, Bagnères-de-Luchon

new.title: Taste plum brioche at Mademoiselle Myrtille
new.desc: This pastry shop and tearoom in Saint-Antonin-Noble-Val sells viennoiseries and brioches flavoured with local blueberry and Saint-Antonin plum on Sunday mornings. It also stocks bread from a Caylus bakery and chocolate from a Najac maker.
new.tip: Go on Sunday morning for the flavoured brioches.
new.q: Mademoiselle Myrtille Pâtisserie Salon de thé, 7 place du Buoc, Saint-Antonin-Noble-Val

new.title: Share plates and natural wine at Vigne en Foule, Gaillac
new.desc: Vigne en Foule on Place de la Libération is a Michelin Bib Gourmand bistro with revisited cooking, shared meat plates and nearly 300 wine references in the cellar.
new.tip: Order a Gaillac wine by the glass. Book for dinner.
new.q: Vigne en Foule, Place de la Libération, Gaillac

new.title: Eat azinat with rouzole at Le P'tit Montagnard in Ax
new.desc: Le P'tit Montagnard on Place Roussel serves azinat, a cabbage stew with its rouzole meat patty, and the Ariège cassoulet called mounjetado. In winter it also offers fondue and tartiflette.
new.tip: Warming after a thermal footbath at the nearby Bassin des Ladres.
new.q: Le P'tit Montagnard, Place Roussel, Ax-les-Thermes

new.title: Buy pink-garlic condiments at La Ferme au Village, Lautrec
new.desc: This boutique in Lautrec has reinvented local products since 1996, making condiments with vinegar and Ail Rose de Lautrec, which has held the Label Rouge since 1966 and an IGP.
new.tip: Also sells online. Buy a jar of pink-garlic condiment.
new.q: La Ferme au Village, Lautrec

new.title: Taste local products at Le Terroir du Père Barras, Cordes
new.desc: Le Terroir du Père Barras is a tasting shop of regional products in Cordes-sur-Ciel, listed by the regional tourism board as a tasting address.
new.tip: Combine with the Grand Rue walk; check hours as they vary by season.
new.q: Le Terroir du Père Barras, 14 Grand Rue Raimond VII, Cordes-sur-Ciel

new.title: Eat farm produce at La Grange de la Cité, Saint-Lizier
new.desc: La Grange de la Cité at 17 rue Maubec is a farm restaurant and tearoom whose boutique sells syrups, spreads, jams and pickles processed from the farm's organic market gardening.
new.tip: Reserve for lunch. Visit after the cloister.
new.q: La Grange de la Cité, 17 Rue Maubec, Saint-Lizier

new.title: Have a grill at Café de la Paix in Luchon
new.desc: The Café de la Paix is a long-established brasserie on the Allées d'Etigny with a menu of grilled meats, fish, oysters and south-west recipes.
new.tip: Take a terrace table on the tree-lined Allées d'Etigny.
new.q: Café de la Paix, Allées d'Etigny, Bagnères-de-Luchon

new.title: Dine at Le Festin de Babette above the Aveyron
new.desc: Le Festin de Babette is on the Marsac road at Saint-Antonin-Noble-Val with a terrace above the Aveyron, open Wednesday to Sunday for lunch and Friday and Saturday evenings from February to November.
new.tip: Reserve a terrace table in summer.
new.q: Le Festin de Babette, Route de Marsac, Saint-Antonin-Noble-Val

new.title: Sweat in the natural Vaporarium of the Thermes de Luchon
new.desc: The Thermes de Luchon is the spa of the Pyrenean town of Bagnères-de-Luchon. Its Vaporarium is described as a natural hammam carved into the rock.
new.tip: Book a session online. Combine with a half-day at Superbagnères.
new.q: Thermes de Luchon, Allées d'Etigny, Bagnères-de-Luchon

new.title: Ride up to Superbagnères above Luchon
new.desc: A gondola has linked Luchon with the Superbagnères ski area since 1993, and a newer Crémaillère Express opened in 2024. The plateau has 32 km of runs and a Tour de France climb.
new.tip: A day pass cost around 36 euros in 2025-26. Cyclists climb the Tour de France road.
new.q: Télécabine de Superbagnères, Bagnères-de-Luchon

new.title: Hike to the Lac d'Oô from the Granges d'Astau
new.desc: The walk starts at the Granges d'Astau, the road end past the village of Oô, and follows the GR 10 to the lake below a 275-metre waterfall. The refuge sits at 1,505 metres.
new.tip: About two hours round trip. A summer shuttle links Luchon with the Granges d'Astau.
new.q: Granges d'Astau, Oô

new.title: Walk to the Cascade du Cœur in the Vallée du Lys
new.desc: A short family out-and-back of about 1.6 km and 50 minutes starts from the car park in the Vallée du Lys near Luchon. The return can be extended to the Cascade d'Enfer.
new.tip: The road to the Hospice de France is closed from 30 November to mid-April.
new.q: Parking de la Vallée du Lys, Bagnères-de-Luchon

new.title: Walk the loop around the Saint-Ferréol lake
new.desc: A circuit leaves from Revel around the Bassin de Saint-Ferréol, the reservoir built in the 1660s for the Canal du Midi. The lake is now a leisure park.
new.tip: Visorando lists the loop; allow two hours. The lake is shaded.
new.q: Bassin de Saint-Ferréol, Revel

new.title: Browse the Saturday market under Revel's hall
new.desc: Revel holds a Saturday morning market under its medieval covered hall, described by guides as one of the finest in France, with local producers' stalls.
new.tip: Saturday mornings only. Arrive early; the belfry visit has been offered on market mornings.
new.q: Halle de Revel, Place Philippe VI de Valois, Revel

new.title: Join the Monday market in Mirepoix
new.desc: The Monday morning market transforms the Place des Couverts and the adjoining streets of the medieval bastide.
new.tip: Monday mornings only. Buy Ariège cheeses and charcuterie.
new.q: Place des Couverts, Mirepoix

new.title: Celebrate at the Lautrec pink garlic festival
new.desc: Lautrec's annual garlic festival takes place on the first Friday of August. The ail rose has held a Label Rouge since 1966 and an IGP since 1996.
new.tip: First Friday of August only; arrive early for stalls and meals.
new.q: Halle de Lautrec, Lautrec

new.title: Walk the Sentier des Merveilles to the Roc de l'Oie
new.desc: The Roc de l'Oie, a goose-shaped granite block, stands on the Sentier des Merveilles that starts at Crémaussel in the Sidobre, east of Castres.
new.tip: Wear good shoes; the boulder fields are uneven.
new.q: Crémaussel, Sidobre, Lacrouzette

new.title: Follow the Ambialade heritage trail at Ambialet
new.desc: A walking heritage trail of about 3.5 km covers the Ambialet peninsula and climbs along the Stations of the Cross toward the priory with views of the Tarn meander.
new.tip: Free access year-round; allow two hours.
new.q: Ambialet, Ambialet

new.title: Soak your feet in the thermal pools of Ax-les-Thermes
new.desc: Free open-air footbaths such as the Bassin des Ladres and the Bassin de La Basse of 1672 let visitors soak in thermal water. The paid spas also offer day entry to indoor and outdoor pools, hammam and sauna.
new.tip: The footbaths are free; the spas charge for day entry.
new.q: Bassin de La Basse, Ax-les-Thermes

new.title: Sail or swim at Lac de Montbel
new.desc: The lake straddles Ariège and Aude, has regular winds for sailing and supervised beaches at Léran and Montbel in summer. Canoe, paddle, pedalo and windsurfing are on offer.
new.tip: Supervised swimming runs roughly 15 June to 15 August. Rent boats at the Léran sailing club.
new.q: Rives de Léran, Lac de Montbel, Léran

new.title: Ride the Labouiche underground river by boat
new.desc: This guided boat trip follows an underground river for nearly 1.5 km, 60 metres below ground. It was discovered in 1908 and opened to the public in 1938. The visit lasts about 75 minutes.
new.tip: Wear closed shoes and a warm layer as it is 13 degrees inside. About 200 steps; check hours.
new.q: Rivière souterraine de Labouiche, Vernajoul, Foix

new.title: Take a gabarre cruise on the Tarn at Albi
new.desc: Albi Croisières runs traditional flat-bottomed gabarres from the banks below the Palais de la Berbie and the Pont-Vieux. Short culture cruises show the town, its bridges and ramparts.
new.tip: Season ran 1 May to 27 September 2026; some trips are by reservation only.
new.q: Albi Croisières, Embarcadère Quai Choiseul, Albi

new.title: Paddle the Gorges de l'Aveyron from Saint-Antonin
new.desc: Several operators at Saint-Antonin-Noble-Val rent canoes and kayaks for routes through the Aveyron gorges, such as a 12 km run to Cazals or a 19 km day to Penne.
new.tip: Rentals run mainly May to September. Book in July and August.
new.q: Cap Canoë Aveyron, Pont de Saint-Antonin, Saint-Antonin-Noble-Val

new.title: Join a wine tasting at the Maison des Vins de Gaillac
new.desc: The Maison des Vins de Gaillac is inside the Abbaye Saint-Michel on the banks of the Tarn. It runs tasting workshops, including a summer initiation with five wines and wine-and-cheese sessions.
new.tip: Reserve by phone or email; the summer 2026 course was listed at 25 euros.
new.q: Maison des Vins de Gaillac, Abbaye Saint-Michel, Place Saint-Michel, Gaillac

new.title: Cycle the Canal du Midi locks from Ayguesvives to Gardouch
new.desc: A return route of about 21.6 km follows the towpath through five locks including Négra, with its small port and chapel, and Gardouch.
new.tip: Start at the Ayguesvives lock car park; lunch at the Gardouch lock.
new.q: Écluse d'Ayguesvives, Canal du Midi, Ayguesvives

new.title: Cycle over the Cacor canal bridge at Moissac
new.desc: The Canal latéral à la Garonne crosses the Tarn at Moissac on the 13-arch Cacor pont-canal, and the towpath is a greenway of the Canal des 2 Mers à vélo.
new.tip: The Moissac to Montauban stage is about 36 km.
new.q: Pont-canal du Cacor, Moissac

new.title: Hike the Sentier du Patrimoine from Puycelsi
new.desc: The Heritage Trail of Puycelsi links the village's conservation orchard to the oak forests of the Grésigne, on footpath only. A very short family variant starts from the tourist office car park.
new.tip: Paths can be poorly marked after rain; carry a GPS.
new.q: Office de tourisme de Puycelsi, Puycelsi

new.title: Walk the Sentier de la Baronne from Castelnau-de-Montmiral
new.desc: An 8 km circuit starts from Castelnau-de-Montmiral and passes the forest house of La Grande Baraque in the Grésigne.
new.tip: Carry water; follow the Cirkwi route.
new.q: Castelnau-de-Montmiral, Castelnau-de-Montmiral
